text.paragraph: Three-month review: lithium, thyroid, kidney and metabolic checks, and the diagnosis reviewed. [S]

Ms. Fitzgerald returns three months after her first visit, fasting for her blood tests. She stopped risperidone eight weeks ago and takes aripiprazole 10 mg each morning and lithium 300 mg twice daily. She had a few days of mild inner restlessness in the first week of the switch, which passed. Her period returned in mid-July, five weeks after the switch, and again this month. She has had no manic, depressive, or psychotic symptoms since the spring and sleeps eight hours. She dances about three hours a day and eats to the dietitian's plan. Since the last visit, with her consent, her roommate and her own journal have filled in the weeks before the admission: the sleeplessness, rapid speech and grand plans came first, for about three weeks, and the voice and the belief she was being watched began only in the last week before admission and ended with the mania. She has had no thoughts of suicide or self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-08-10; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 51.6 kg, BMI 19.0; blood pressure 108/68, pulse 70
Faint fine postural tremor; no akathisia, rigidity, or abnormal movements
Euthymic; organized; no psychotic or manic features

First episode of psychosis with marked mood symptoms: about three weeks of little sleep, rapid speech, racing thoughts, grandiose plans and very long training days, then a voice commenting on her dancing and a belief that she was being watched and tested; tearful low mood since discharge. Diagnosis provisional; differential: bipolar I disorder with psychotic features, schizoaffective disorder (bipolar type), and schizophreniform disorder or schizophrenia, depending on whether the psychosis ever occurred apart from the mood symptoms. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented first hospitalization

S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented first breakdown. Unspecified psychosis is coded until the course shows how the psychosis relates to the mood symptoms; superseded at the three-month visit.

Bipolar I disorder, most recent episode manic with psychotic features, in full remission: the working diagnosis at three months, when her history, her journal, and her roommate's account (given with her consent) showed that the voice and the belief she was watched began only after weeks of manic symptoms and ended with them, with no psychosis since. Remains provisional: it would be revised to schizoaffective disorder if psychosis ever lasted two weeks or more without a mood episode. Synthetic modern episode linked to the documented breakdown and its retrospective interpretations
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made from the course; the historical diagnoses stay in the claims.
Secondary amenorrhea: no periods for about four months before admission, during very heavy dance training at a low weight (BMI 18.7), with prolactin raised on risperidone; pregnancy test negative
S — Synthetic presenting finding linked to her documented training; resolved when her periods returned.
Acute viral gastroenteritis (vomiting and watery diarrhea for two days, roommate with the same illness), with mild dehydration; resolved
S — Synthetic acute infection; not a historical claim.
Lithium level above the therapeutic range (1.4 mmol/L) during dehydration, with nausea and a worse fine tremor, without confusion or unsteadiness; lithium held and restarted; resolved
S — Synthetic medication adverse effect at a prescribed dose; ICD-10-CM classifies lithium salts with the other antipsychotics and neuroleptics.

list.item:
Bipolar I disorder with psychotic features, in full remission (F31.74). The course now settles the provisional diagnosis. The psychotic symptoms occurred only within a manic episode and ended with it, which fits bipolar I disorder with psychotic features rather than schizoaffective disorder, which needs psychosis for two weeks or more without mood symptoms, or schizophrenia. Mood has been normal for about two months, so the illness is in full remission. The label will be revised if psychosis ever occurs apart from a mood episode. Lithium 0.74 mmol/L; creatinine 0.80 mg/dL, eGFR 102; TSH 2.9 mIU/L; calcium 9.6 mg/dL. The 12-week metabolic check is normal: fasting glucose 86 mg/dL, A1c 5.1%, total cholesterol 174, LDL 94, HDL 62 and triglycerides 82 mg/dL. Dr. Langford reviewed the history by phone and agrees. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm; the safety plan is current. [S]
Continue lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily and aripiprazole 10 mg daily.
Lithium level, creatinine and TSH again at six months.
Pregnancy planning: lithium carries a small added risk of heart defects early in pregnancy, valproate is avoided, and any pregnancy should be planned with psychiatry; she would like a long-acting method placed at the preventive visit.

First episode of psychosis with marked mood symptoms (F29). Superseded by the diagnosis of bipolar I disorder with psychotic features. [S]
Problem resolved.

Secondary amenorrhea (N91.1). Resolved: prolactin 14 ng/mL on aripiprazole, periods regular, and energy intake matched to training. [S]
Keep the dietitian's plan as training increases; report any missed period.
